content:
iPadOS and macOS have long been distinctly different software platforms. But since iPadOS 26, the two have grown increasingly similar. This year that's even more apparent, as iPadOS 27 adds three features that bring the iPad closer to the Mac than ever before.

#1: Status Bar Shows App Name

I'm using my M5 iPad Pro with a Magic Keyboard attached all day. The iPad has long had a problem for keyboard users: the lack of a clear "current app" indicator.

If there's only one app on screen, this isn't a problem. But if you're showing multiple apps at once, keyboard shortcuts become very tricky to operate. I can't count how many times I've thought a shortcut would trigger in one app, only to discover it was targeting another.

The Mac solved this long ago by displaying the name of the current app in the top-left corner of the screen. Now, iPadOS 27 follows suit.

iPadOS 27 users will find the name of the current app displayed right alongside other status bar elements like the time and date. It's a small but delightful change that makes the keyboard-equipped iPad experience much more pleasant.

#2: Permanent Menu Bar

Another welcome iPadOS 27 change is the option to permanently display the menu bar.

Last year, Apple first introduced the menu bar to the iPad. But unlike on the Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appeared when the user explicitly summoned it.

In iPadOS 27, a new toggle has been added under "Multitasking & Gestures" in the Settings app, labelled: "Auto-show and hide menu bar".

With this toggle turned off, the menu bar stays visible at all times. Throughout the iPadOS beta period, I've been using my iPad this way, and it's one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Mac-like Everyday Performance

As much as I love my iPad and appreciate the new features it's gained in iPadOS 26 and 27, I still get frustrated at times by the sluggishness of basic operations. For instance, I wrote earlier this year: "Right-clicking in iPadOS often feels slow and laggy, whereas on the Mac it happens instantly."

Thanks to Apple's bug-fixing focus this year, I'm happy to report that iPadOS 27 brings speed improvements to these kinds of everyday operations.

Apple says right-click menus now open faster when using a cursor, and I can certainly feel it. Browsing files and transferring them to an external drive is now "up to 5× faster," according to Apple, making it as quick as Finder on the Mac. App launches are more responsive, and window management is snappier when closing, switching, or dragging windows.

There are still areas where the Mac is faster and the iPad feels sluggish. But overall, the performance upgrades in iPadOS 27 are a significant step in the right direction.

What are your favourite new features and changes in iPadOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
